title: Append-only customer consumption ledger: delta Parquet shipments + idempotent webhook ack
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem context:
Customers increasingly require incremental, auditable, and resumable consumption exports for reconciliation and analytics. Our current CSV scheduled-exports and ad-hoc S3 delivery paths are brittle for large tenants: they generate heavy duplicate payloads, have poor resume semantics, and don’t scale well to high change rates or retention-aware deletes (GDPR).

Goals:
- Deliver an append-only consumption ledger per tenant as compact delta Parquet shipments with a small JSON manifest chain that describes base+delta relationships.
- Provide strong delivery semantics for webhook consumers: idempotent delivery using ordered sequence tokens and explicit ack handshake to avoid duplicates and enable backpressure.
- Maintain backward compatibility with scheduled CSV exports (migration path), and offer an opt-in parity mode for existing customers.
- Observable, debuggable pipeline with per-tenant delivery metrics, DLQ for failed deliveries, and reconciliation hooks for billing.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Ingestion/ledger: Consolidate per-tenant usage events into an append-only ledger (time-partitioned). We compact periodically into delta Parquet files (daily/hourly depending on tenant size) and emit a manifest.json that lists base_parquet_uri, delta_uris[], sequence_range, checksum, and retention_cutoff.
2) Shipping: A delivery worker reads manifests and attempts to deliver the minimal set of new deltas to the configured sink (S3/GCS signed url or webhook). For webhooks we implement a three-way handshake: POST /deliver -> receiver returns 202 with expected-seq or 409+retry-after; on success the receiver returns 200 with ack{sequence_received}. The delivery worker marks sequences acknowledged atomically in our ledger index.
3) Idempotency & ordering: Every webhook delivery includes ledger_id, sequence_start, sequence_end, and idempotency_token. Receivers must store idempotency_token and respond with the last accepted sequence to allow resumability. Delivery workers implement exactly-once semantics best-effort: retries are idempotent; duplicates are suppressed by receiver acking.
4) Backpressure & DLQ: If receiver returns structured backpressure (429/503 with retry-after or 409 for reordering), worker will back off per-tenant with exponential jitter and move older payloads into a bounded in-cluster queue. After N retries (configurable per-tier), payloads are moved to DLQ S3 with metadata and a human-visible Dashboard alert.
5) Schema evolution & validation: Parquet schemas are versioned in the manifest. Consumers can request a specific schema version. We include an on-delivery schema-compatibility check and fail-fast for breaking incompatible writes.
6) Migration & compatibility: Provide a compatibility layer that can produce traditional CSV scheduled exports from the same ledger (materialize view) while customers opt-in to delta parity on a tenant-by-tenant basis.

Trade-offs considered:
- Using Parquet reduces size and read cost but increases complexity for small customers who prefer CSV; hence the compatibility layer.
- Exactly-once across networks is impossible without receiver cooperation; we design for idempotent delivery with explicit acks and best-effort suppression of duplicates.
- Maintaining ordered delivery can increase latency for tenants with slow receivers; we surface per-tenant delivery SLOs and allow per-tenant delivery concurrency settings.

Operational plan:
- Phase 1: Prototype delta manifest format and idempotent webhook handshake in a staging job (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: Implement delivery worker, DLQ, and observability (metrics, per-tenant graph) and run canary against internal tenants (4 weeks).
- Phase 3: Migrate a small set of external customers behind feature flag and validate billing reconciliation (3 weeks).
- Phase 4: Gradual rollout and CSV compatibility migration tooling (3 weeks).

acceptance_criteria: End-to-end pipeline produces per-tenant manifest + delta Parquet artifacts in staging and a test webhook consumer can resume from any manifest without data loss
Webhooks use idempotency_token and receiver ack semantics; we observe zero duplicate rows in consumer tests after 10k simulated retries
DLQ contains original manifest + payload and an automated alert fires for >95th percentile retry latency per-tenant
CSV compatibility layer can generate a faithful CSV snapshot from the same ledger for a sample tenant and costs are within 1.5x of current CSV job for small tenants
Reconciliation job matches exported usage vs billing ledger within 0.1% for test dataset
